To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
intercultural communication systems are hegemonic structures, which produce discourses of cultural identity and that intercultural dialogue is an alternative to these discourses.
the meaning of cultural identities is constructed in communication systems, which are based on their particular structures and presuppositions.

intercultural communication can be explained as an interdependent system of communication systems, in which the hegemonic structure is ethnocentrin, and that intercultural dialogue is a discursive construction of intercultural hegemony.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the meaning of the discursive and epistemological foundations of intercultural dialogues.
the analysis of the meaning of cultural variability, identity, and dialogue, which is produced in communication systems, and with the identification of the presuppositions of their structures.

intercultural communication as a discursive process of identity construction, based on the presuppositions of cultural variability, and with dialogue as an alternative to the hegemonic construction of cultural identities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
intercultural dialogue is a new discursive structure of interculturality.
intercultural communication systems and dialogic communication systems are not two different systems, but two different ways of describing the same system.

this paper proposes a theorisation of intercultural systems of communication as an alternative explanation of cultural differences and identity in the global world, which can be adopted as a basis for the development of intercultural education.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are not interested in the question of what is the best intercultural communication system or the best interculturality.
the present analysis of inter-cultural communication is based on a form epistemological essentialist, produced in the western part of the world, to give meaning to hegemony.

intercultural communication systems, based on ethnocentrism and the hegemonic structure, are the main source of cultural differences and the discursive construction, which gives meaning to the present world.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we need to develop new theories to explain the meaning, the structure, and the functions of intercultural dialogues in the global world.

intercultural communication systems can be analysed as structures of communication, which are based on particular structural presuppositions and which are used to give meaning to cultural differences and identities.
the study of intercultural communicative practices should be informed by an understanding of the discursive constructions of cultural identity.
